subject: Post-call recap: model recommendations, perf profiles & links
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@brightline.health>, Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@brightline.health>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 02 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: model recommendations, perf profiles & links

Hi Liam & Sofia,

Thanks again for taking time earlier — really valuable context on Brightline's triage flow and latency targets. Quick recap and the follow-ups we promised:

Summary of requirements (from call)
- Latency target: 200ms p90 for short-turn clarifying prompts (<=128 tokens)
- Quality target: high factuality for medical guidance, low hallucination tolerance
- Traffic: start with ~40 TPS bursty, steady at ~10–15 TPS; expected growth to ~120 TPS over 6–9 months
- Security: VPC/private deployment preferred for PHI; SOC2 evidence required

High-level model recommendations (tradeoffs)
- Latency-first (cost-efficient): rw-13b-v1-quant (4-bit) — good p50/p90 for interactive flows, strong for short prompts; recommended for chat front-ends and realtime clarifications.
- Quality-first (higher compute): rw-70b-v1-4bit — better instruction following and medical nuance; use for synthesis/clinical summary tasks where latency SLO is relaxed.
- Hybrid approach: route short clarifying prompts to rw-13b-v1-quant, fall back to rw-70b-v1-4bit for synthesis or low-confidence outputs (we can manage automatic routing in the platform).

Redwood-verified performance (representative, measured on H100-lp cluster):
- rw-13b-v1-quant @ seq=128: throughput ~48 TPS (single-model pool), p50 ~85ms, p90 ~190ms, p99 ~410ms
- rw-70b-v1-4bit @ seq=256: throughput ~11 TPS, p50 ~240ms, p90 ~510ms, p99 ~950ms
Notes: these are lab measurements with prefix KV caching enabled and continuous batching tuned for low latency workloads. We'll run a Brightline-specific run with your sample prompts to generate exact numbers.

What we're sharing now
- Redwood-verified perf profiles for the recommended variants (attached PDF)
- A link to an eval bundle with the prompt sets we discussed: https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-evals/brightline/prompt-sets.zip
- Quickstart to run the local eval harness + instructions: https://console.redwood.ai/perf/brightline-2026

Immediate next steps / asks from Brightline
1) Share a 2–3k sample of real prompts/examples (de-identified) so we run the same evals on your distribution — helps validate p90/p99.
2) Decision on deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC). For PHI, Private is recommended; we can provision a Private eval cluster.
3) Confirm a 60‑minute architecture workshop next week (we propose Tue 8/4 10:00–11:00 PT).

I'll loop Dev for the technical perf run and Marcus to scope the Mutual Action Plan. I attached a starter MAP and the PDF perf profiles.

Thanks — Neha

Hi Liam / Neha — looping in from the infra/serving side with a few concrete items and the lab run plan.

Short answers to Liam's Qs:
- Cost delta: rough ballpark (on Hosted API pricing) at 15 TPS steady: routing primarily to rw-13b-v1-quant is ~35–45% of the cost of using rw-70b for all requests. Exact numbers depend on token lengths and cache hit rate. We'll produce a cost projection with your sample prompts.
- Regression detection: Redwood Optimize supports prompt-set-based monitoring (you upload a labeled prompt set + expected outputs); we run nightly signal checks and produce quality drift alerts. For canary model rollouts we run the gate using your medical test suite (we can integrate your safety checks).
- Private eval lead time: for a small Private eval cluster we can provision in ~7–10 business days once infra details + PO are in place. Dedicated reserved capacity is longer (2–4 weeks) for production.

Planned lab run (what we'll deliver in 48 hours once we get the full sample):
1) Ingest your sample prompts into the Redwood eval harness (we already have the file you attached).
2) Run 3 variants: rw-13b-v1-quant, rw-13b-v1-int8 (if you want lower cost but slightly higher latency), rw-70b-v1-4bit.
3) Capture: throughput (TPS) under synthetic concurrency, p50/p90/p99 latencies, token-level cost, and a per-prompt quality score using your labels (where available).
4) Deliverables: CSV perf dump, per-prompt diffs, suggested routing policy and batch/caching params.

Representative lab numbers (different hardware/environment than your eventual Private cluster — we'll re-run against yours):
- rw-13b-v1-quant (H100-lp pool) — seq=128: TPS 48; p50 85ms; p90 190ms; p99 410ms
- rw-13b-v1-int8 (H100) — seq=128: TPS 36; p50 110ms; p90 260ms; p99 520ms
- rw-70b-v1-4bit (H100-lp) — seq=256: TPS 11; p50 240ms; p90 510ms; p99 950ms

Notes on configuration that materially affect numbers:
- Prefix/KV caching: for flows with repeated context (patient history, triage prompts), enabling prefix caching reduces p90 by ~20–40% in our tests.
- Batching: continuous batching increases throughput but add a few ms to p50; we configure per-route batching to meet p90 SLOs.

I'll kick off the eval run once Neha confirms we have permission to run the attached sample at the scale described.

Action items (owner):
- Brightline: send full sample dump + confirm Private vs Hosted (Liam) — due 8/5
- Redwood: run eval harness + send CSVs and perf profile (Dev) — target 8/5–8/6
- Redwood Sales: provide MAP and contract starter (Neha / Marcus) — target 8/6

See the perf dashboard here: https://console.redwood.ai/perf/brightline-2026 (we'll add results there).

Thanks,
Dev Patel
